facts.text: A collision mitigation system can pass a finite set of standards tests and still be unusable if false alarms occur every few minutes or unexpected braking occurs several times a shift; the absence of false-alarm and unnecessary-brake rates is therefore consequential.
facts.quote: a system can pass a finite set of standards tests and still be unusable if it alarms every few minutes or brakes unexpectedly several times a shift.

facts.text: A program-level collision mitigation acceptance specification should measure at least scenario-conditioned true-positive detection and intervention, dangerous misses, false warnings per operating hour, unnecessary interventions per operating hour, and collision-avoidance rate.
facts.quote: measure at least scenario-conditioned true-positive detection and intervention, dangerous misses, false warnings per operating hour, unnecessary interventions per operating hour, collision-avoidance rate

facts.text: A program-level collision mitigation acceptance specification should also measure residual impact speed, minimum stopping margin, warning lead time, brake-command latency, availability, time in degraded mode and fault-detection coverage.
facts.quote: residual impact speed, minimum stopping margin, warning lead time, brake-command latency, availability, time in degraded mode and fault-detection coverage

facts.text: A program-level collision mitigation acceptance specification should set separate tolerances for advisory warnings, urgent warnings, speed-reduction commands and full brake interventions.
facts.quote: with separate tolerances for advisory warnings, urgent warnings, speed-reduction commands and full brake interventions

facts.text: An unnecessary advisory warning is not equivalent to an unnecessary emergency stop of a loaded machine when setting collision mitigation acceptance tolerances.
facts.quote: an unnecessary advisory is not equivalent to an unnecessary emergency stop of a loaded machine.

facts.text: Program-level collision mitigation acceptance values should not be presented as mandated by ISO unless a normative clause supplies those values.
facts.quote: None of these values should be presented as mandated by ISO unless the normative clause supplies them.
